messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Streaming p99 latency SLO breached for /v1/stream (prod). p95=320ms, p99=2.8s, error-budget burn 45% in 10m. Severity: SEV2. Pager: mike_oncall
mike_oncall: I'm on it. Observability link?
incident-bot: https://grafana.company/reports/2145/streaming-latency (auto-attached)
liz_support: No incoming customer escalations yet but a partner reported stalls during ~30s streams ~10m ago.
jia_infra: checking infra metrics — seeing a big spike in GPU correctable ECC errors on host gpu-rtg-07 (node rtc-07). Correctable errors/sec jumped from ~3 to ~620 at 21:07 UTC. Also intermittent PCIe resets in dmesg.
alex_sre: can you paste the node logs?
jia_infra: logs clipped below:
```
[21:06:52] nvidia 0000:3b:00.0: GPU ECC error corrected (count=1)
[21:07:01] nvidia 0000:3b:00.0: GPU ECC error corrected (count=245)
[21:07:12] nvidia 0000:3b:00.0: thermal warning: 89C
[21:07:55] kernel: PCIe link reset on 0000:3b:00.0
```
mike_oncall: nvpeer, thermal + ECC + resets -> likely flaky card causing stalls and increased scheduler latency for streaming tasks. Impact path: streaming keeps long KV cache in GPU; when a GPU stalls the runtime retries tokens, p99 balloons.
sara_ops: any automatic fallback triggered?
deploy-bot: Router policy: fallback to model-ht-medium triggered after 21:09:23 for affected instances. Traffic rerouted: ~18% of requests.
alex_sre: immediate mitigation steps I propose:
- cordon & drain gpu-rtg-07
- fail traffic to warm fallback pool (quantized/medium model) to cut tail latency
- throttle burst concurrency for streaming route to reduce retries
- open vendor HW ticket (INC-5483) and attach logs
Can someone run drain?
mike_oncall: running drain now:
```
kubectl cordon rtc-07
kubectl drain rtc-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=10m
```
(keeps some long-lived streams open until they finish, tries to migrate new sessions away)
jia_infra: starting driver unload on rtc-07 and reprovisioning to alternate GPU slot. Also bumping routing weight to fallback pool to 75%.
liz_support: letting top partners know: "We routed your streaming traffic to a lower-latency fallback while we investigate; you may see slightly different sampling/formatting for long streams." Sent to Partner-X and BetaGroup-A.
alex_sre: observed immediate p99 improvement after routing change: p99 dropped to 420ms within 2 minutes, p95 ~290ms. But we still see occasional spikes when some long sessions keep pinned to gpu-rtg-07 pre-drain.
mike_oncall: node drain completed at 21:22 UTC, driver restarted. However nv-host-recovery shows repeated ECC corrections persisted prior to driver restart. I've isolated affected container instances and terminated them to force reschedule.
sara_ops: hardware team pinged and vendor ticket created INC-5483 with nvml logs & dmesg. HW requested full GPU dump and serial numbers.
alex_sre: long-term actions: replace card in rtc-07, add automated GPU ECC alerting to catch correctable error rate >100/min, add auto-evacuate for >5 PCIe resets in 10m.
liz_support: will draft a short customer note if vendor replacement ETA >24h.
incident-bot: Timeline update posted to incident channel. Runbook step applied: streaming-fallback-rule-v3 executed.
mike_oncall: I'm handing off to alex_sre for next shift/monitoring. Key notes: root cause looks hardware-level (ECC + thermal + PCIe resets). Mitigation: drained node, rerouted 75% traffic to fallback quantized model, throttle concurrency on streaming route.
alex_sre: taking over. I'll keep an eye for recurrence and coordinate hardware swap. @jia_infra continue with full card replacement workflow.
jia_infra: started card replacement playbook (rack ticket + vendor onsite). ETA first availability check in 5h. Swapping to hot-spare until then.
mike_oncall: thanks — marking pager clear for me.
alex_sre: watchlist for next 24h: p99, ECC correctables, thermal temps, PCIe resets. Setting alert: p99 > 1.2s -> SEV2 recreate.
sara_ops: created post-incident doc stub and assigned to alex_sre + jia_infra for root-cause and action items. INC-5483 linked.
liz_support: customer comms queued, will hold until we have concrete ETA from HW.
incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Close when hardware replaced and no recurrence for 72h.
alex_sre: acknowledged. Will update thread with vendor RMA and swap notes.
